summary: Thin but source-faithful decomposition of the coherent-sheaf side of this roadmap. Three nodes are written, all from statements read in two sources: the two categories of weights (scalar automorphy factors versus representations of the centralizer of the Hodge cocharacter) and the concrete Levi instantiation; the canonical extension on a toroidal compactification with fan-independent sections, its log connection for bundles restricted from the whole group, and the subcanonical extension as the twist by the reduced boundary divisor, together with the fact that a general automorphic vector bundle does NOT extend over the minimal compactification; and the classical automorphy and growth conditions. One correction is recorded: the source's printed cocycle condition for an automorphy factor is inconsistent with its own automorphy condition, and the atlas stage text has the correct identity. Six of the nine stages (B0, B1, B1.general, B2.general, B3.general, B5) have no nodes (count corrected by the reviewer): the canonical principal bundle, which is the core object of B0 and B1, has no readable source in the supplied library - Deligne's Varietes de Shimura is present but its PDF carries no text layer, and Milne's 1990 automorphic-vector-bundles paper is absent from the catalogue.

nodes.title: The classical definition of a modular form by an automorphy factor, and the cocycle identity it forces
nodes.statement: In the source's classical formulation, a holomorphic modular form is a holomorphic f: D -> C satisfying (1) the AUTOMORPHY CONDITION f(gamma Z) = j(gamma, Z) f(Z) for all gamma in Gamma and Z in D, for an automorphy factor j: Gamma x D -> C^* defining the weight of f; and (2) the GROWTH CONDITION that f(Z) stays bounded near D^* minus D, with f a cusp form when in addition f(Z) -> 0 as Z -> D^* minus D. When Gamma is neat, the growth condition implies that the section represented by f extends to a section of a line bundle over the minimal compactification (Gamma\D)^min = Gamma\D^*. The automorphy factor is exactly the datum making f a section of an automorphic line bundle over Gamma\D; the line bundles used in the classical embedding theorem are powers of the canonical bundle, i.e. the top exterior power of the cotangent bundle of Gamma\D. CORRECTION TO THE SOURCE: the source displays the cocycle condition as j(gamma' gamma, Z) = j(gamma', Z) j(gamma, Z). That is inconsistent with its own automorphy condition: applying the automorphy condition twice gives f(gamma' gamma Z) = j(gamma', gamma Z) f(gamma Z) = j(gamma', gamma Z) j(gamma, Z) f(Z), so the correct identity for a LEFT action is j(gamma' gamma, Z) = j(gamma', gamma Z) j(gamma, Z). The reviewer confirmed the printed form on the page image of p. 49 (300 dpi): it reads j(gamma' gamma, Z) = j(gamma', Z) j(gamma, Z), so this is a typo in the source and not an extraction artefact. (The drafted evidence, two text extractions from the same text layer, could not by itself exclude an artefact.) The atlas stage text for B4 states the correct identity.
hypotheses: the growth condition's consequence - extension of the section over the minimal compactification - is stated only when Gamma is NEAT

the automorphy factor takes values in C^*, so this formulation captures only LINE bundles; vector-valued weights need automorphy factors valued in the centralizer of h_0 in G(C), which is treated separately
the cocycle identity as printed in the source is wrong; the correct left-action identity carries the argument gamma Z in the first factor
the atlas stage text further requires deriving the RIGHT-action formula rather than reusing the left-action one; no source read here does that derivation
proofSteps: The source states the two conditions and the cocycle condition in its Section 4.2.7.
The inconsistency is detected by composing the automorphy condition with itself, which is the only way the two displayed conditions can be reconciled.
acceptance: Verify the cocycle identity by composing the automorphy condition twice, and check that the printed form fails already for SL_2(Z) acting on the upper half plane with j(gamma, z) = (cz+d)^k
Check that for non-neat Gamma the growth condition does not by itself give extension across the minimal compactification

sources.excerpt: (1) Automorphy condition: f (γZ) = j(γ, Z)f (Z), for all γ ∈ Γ and Z ∈ D, for some automorphy factor j : Γ × D → C× defining the weight of f , satisfying the cocycle condition j(γ 0 γ, Z) = j(γ 0 , Z)j(γ, Z) for all γ, γ 0 ∈ Γ and Z ∈ D.

sources.excerpt: (2) Growth condition: f (Z) stays bounded near D∗ − D. (When Γ is neat, this implies that the section represented by f extends to a section of a line bundle over (Γ\D) min = Γ\D∗ .) If f satisfies the additional condition that f (Z) → 0 as Z → D ∗ − D, then f is called a cusp form.
sources.match: The growth condition with the neatness hypothesis attached to its geometric consequence.

nodes.title: Canonical and subcanonical extensions on a toroidal compactification, and why the minimal one does not work
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional representation W of the centralizer of h_0 in G(C) the associated automorphic vector bundle W over Gamma\D in general does NOT extend to a vector bundle over the minimal compactification (Gamma\D)^min; the source notes this is consistent with the boundary of the minimal compactification having high codimension. It does, however, admit CANONICAL EXTENSIONS W^can to vector bundles over the toroidal compactifications (Gamma\D)^tor_Sigma, whose SECTIONS ARE INDEPENDENT OF Sigma. When W is the restriction of a representation of the whole group G(C), the bundle W carries an integrable connection, and W^can carries an integrable connection WITH LOG POLES along the boundary, coinciding with the one of Deligne's canonical extension. The SUBCANONICAL extension is W^sub = W^can(-infinity), where infinity denotes the boundary divisor (Gamma\D)^tor minus (Gamma\D) with its REDUCED structure; its global sections are, in the source's words, '(roughly speaking) useful for studying cusp forms' (reviewer correction of the drafted 'are what is used for cusp forms'; the precise identification with cusp forms is stated in the second source for its setting). The cohomology of W^can and W^sub is the coherent cohomology of the toroidal compactification, and it is this algebro-geometric formulation that permits modular forms in mixed or positive characteristic over integral models. The same construction appears in the unitary-similitude setting of the second source: a locally free E_{U,rho} on X_{n,U} with canonical locally free extension E_{U,Delta,rho} to the smooth compactification X_{n,U,Delta} whose boundary is a simple normal crossings divisor, and E^sub_{U,Delta,rho} = the product of E_{U,Delta,rho} with the ideal sheaf of the boundary, whose global sections are the holomorphic cusp forms of weight rho and level U - again independent of Delta.
hypotheses: the canonical extension is on a TOROIDAL compactification and depends on a choice of admissible fan Sigma (resp. auxiliary data Delta); only the SPACES OF SECTIONS are independent of that choice, not the sheaf
the log connection is available only for W restricted from a representation of the whole group G(C), not for an arbitrary representation of the centralizer
the subcanonical extension is the twist by the ideal sheaf of the REDUCED boundary divisor; the reducedness is part of the definition
in the second source the compactification is required to be SMOOTH with simple normal crossings boundary; the canonical extension is asserted locally free there
proofSteps: The first source states the non-extension over the minimal compactification, the existence of the canonical extension with Sigma-independent sections, the log connection, and the definition of the subcanonical extension, citing Mumford and Harris for the canonical extension and Deligne for the connection.
The second source repeats the construction concretely for its unitary-similitude Shimura varieties and records the independence from Delta twice - once for automorphic forms and once for cusp forms.
acceptance: Check on a modular curve that the canonical extension of the weight-k bundle is omega^k on the compactified curve and the subcanonical extension is omega^k(-cusps)
Exhibit a representation W of the centralizer whose automorphic bundle does not extend over the minimal compactification, confirming that the toroidal compactification is necessary
Check that the log connection exists for W restricted from G(C). The source asserts nothing for a general W, so do not test that it fails there (reviewer correction)

sources.excerpt: Nevertheless, the automorphic vector bundle W has canonical extensions (see [Mum77] and [Har89]) to vector bundles W can over the toroidal compactifications (Γ\D)tor Σ , whose sections are independent of Σ.
sources.match: The canonical extension with the Sigma-independence of its sections, which the stage requires to be proved rather than assumed.

sources.excerpt: (When W is the restriction of a representation of G(C), the vector bundle W is equipped with an integrable connection, and its canonical extension W can is equipped with an integrable connection with log poles along the boundary and coincides with the one given in [Del70].)
sources.match: The log-connection statement with its exact hypothesis - W restricted from the whole group - which the stage names.

sources.excerpt: There are also the subcanonical extensions W sub := W can (−∞), where ∞ abusively denotes the boundary divisor (Γ\D)tor − (Γ\D) with its reduced structure, whose global sections are (roughly speaking) useful for studying cusp forms.
sources.match: The definition of the subcanonical extension with the reduced boundary divisor.

sources.excerpt: The product of EU,∆,ρ with the ideal sheaf of the boundary of Xn,U,∆ , which we denote sub EU,∆,ρ , is again locally free and its global sections are holomorphic cusp forms on Gn ‘of weight ρ and level U ’ (and again the space of global sections does not depend on ∆).

nodes.title: The bundle attached to a representation, and the two weight categories that must be distinguished
nodes.statement: Two categories of weights appear and must be kept distinct. (i) Automorphy factors valued in C^* give automorphic LINE bundles, and these are the classical scalar weights. (ii) Automorphy factors valued in the centralizer Cent_{h_0}(G(C)) of the Hodge cocharacter give automorphic VECTOR bundles W for arbitrary finite-dimensional representations W of that centralizer. The source states explicitly that not all modular forms arise from case (i). Bundles in case (ii) coming from representations of the whole group G(C) carry an integrable connection, and their canonical extensions carry a connection with log poles. The source states only this direction; the drafted 'exactly those' and 'only those' are not in it (reviewer correction). The B2 stage text likewise warns against assigning the flat structure to every automorphic bundle. In the second source the corresponding object is a representation rho of the Levi L_{n,(n)} = GL_1 x Res_{F/Q} GL_n of the maximal parabolic of the quasi-split unitary similitude group, with the attached locally free sheaf E_{U,rho} on the Shimura variety X_{n,U} (U neat), whose global sections over the canonical extension are the holomorphic automorphic forms of weight rho and level U.
hypotheses: the group whose representations give weights is the centralizer of h_0 in G(C), i.e. a Levi, not the whole group

the source attaches the integrable connection, and the log connection on the canonical extension, to representations restricted from G(C); it says nothing about other automorphic bundles (reviewer correction of 'is where connections live')
in the concrete unitary-similitude setting the weight group is the Levi of a specific maximal parabolic, and the Shimura variety is NOT proper
the relation between sections of the analytic bundle and the algebro-geometric one is the content of the comparison the stage requires; it is not read here
proofSteps: The first source distinguishes the two weight categories and records the consequence for connections.
The second source instantiates the construction concretely and identifies global sections with automorphic forms of weight rho and level U.
acceptance: Check that the weight category for the modular curve is representations of the standard torus, recovering the classical integer weight

Check that the canonical (Gauss-Manin-type) connection is built from the G(C)-representation. Do not test for the absence of every integrable connection on a bundle whose representation does not extend: on the open modular curve every holomorphic vector bundle is trivial and so carries a flat connection (reviewer correction)

sources.excerpt: Not all modular forms are defined as above using only automorphy factors valued in C× . It is possible to consider automorphy factors valued in Centh0 (G(C)), so that it makes sense to consider modular forms with weights given by all finite-dimensional representations W of Centh0 (G(C)).
sources.match: The two weight categories, with the centralizer of the Hodge cocharacter as the weight group in the vector-valued case.

sources.excerpt: To a representation ρ of Ln,(n) (over Q) one can attach a locally free sheaf EU,ρ /Xn,U together with a canonical (locally free) extension EU,∆,ρ to Xn,U,∆ , whose global sections are holomorphic automorphic forms on Gn ‘of weight ρ and level U ’.
sources.match: The concrete instantiation with the Levi as weight group and the identification of global sections with automorphic forms.

links.reason: The canonical and subcanonical extensions are extensions OF the automorphic vector bundle attached to a representation, so B3 consumes B2's construction; and the availability of a log connection on the canonical extension is conditional on B2's distinction between representations of the centralizer and those restricted from the whole group.

The stage defines classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions and then requires the analytic transformation-law comparison; the growth condition of the classical definition is exactly what corresponds to extension across the boundary, and the source states that correspondence (for neat Gamma) as the consequence of the growth condition. Reviewer annotation: the stage edge is supported by the B4 stage text ('Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions. Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison'). The node-level claim that the source states the correspondence is too strong. What the source states for neat Gamma is that bounded growth makes the section of a LINE bundle extend over the MINIMAL compactification. It says nothing that ties the classical conditions to sections of W^can or W^sub, and that comparison remains unread.

The exact output supplied is the subcanonical extension together with the independence of its spaces of sections from the auxiliary compactification data.

gaps.title: The source's printed cocycle condition for an automorphy factor is wrong
gaps.detail: Verified: the source's Section 4.2.7 displays the automorphy condition f(gamma Z) = j(gamma, Z) f(Z) together with the cocycle condition j(gamma' gamma, Z) = j(gamma', Z) j(gamma, Z). These two are inconsistent: composing the automorphy condition gives f(gamma' gamma Z) = j(gamma', gamma Z) j(gamma, Z) f(Z), so the correct left-action identity is j(gamma' gamma, Z) = j(gamma', gamma Z) j(gamma, Z). The reviewer confirmed the printed string on the page image of p. 49 at 300 dpi, so this is a typo in the source and not an extraction artefact. The drafted check (two text extractions of the same text layer) could not by itself settle that. The atlas stage text for B4 states the correct identity; no correction to the atlas is needed. Next source action: none required for the mathematics; when the packet is promoted, cite a source that prints the identity correctly, for instance any standard treatment of automorphy factors.

review.notes: Additional packet present in the EXT-10 job directory at the start of the review. All 3 nodes and 3 links checked against the library copies of Lan's Example-Based Introduction and HLTT (SHA-256 re-verified). The library and catalogue claims in coverage and gaps were confirmed: Deligne's Varietes de Shimura text file is 43 bytes; Lan's PEL compactifications thesis is present with text; Milne 1990 and Harris on vector bundles are absent. Verdicts: 1 verified, 2 corrected, 0 unverifiable. Main corrections: (1) the source's misprinted cocycle condition was confirmed on the page image (the drafter's evidence was two extractions of the same text layer); (2) the claim that bundles from G(C)-representations are 'exactly' those with integrable connections, and the acceptance test built on it, are not in the source and the test is false (every holomorphic bundle on the open modular curve is trivial); (3) W^sub's sections are 'roughly speaking useful for studying cusp forms' in Lan, not identified with cusp forms; (4) the summary said 'Five' of six unread stages. Links: 2 verified (B2 -> B3; B3 -> AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4, whose stage text imports canonical/subcanonical extensions), 1 annotated (B3 -> B4: the source's growth-condition consequence concerns line bundles over the minimal compactification, not W^can). Gaps 4 (one detail updated). Coverage names real stages; parentStageIds belong to the roadmap; no stage or node cycle. Packet status stays partial.
